videos.script: Open a web page and two programs talk. One of them was already waiting. The other one started the conversation. {{two}} That is the whole difference between a client and a server. It is a difference of role, not of hardware. {{roles}} In this lesson you watch it happen in the office lab. A machine called srv listens on port 80. Three PCs connect to it at the same time, and one command on the server lists all three conversations side by side. {{listing}} You will read each of those lines as four numbers: two addresses and two ports. That is what a connection is. {{tuple}} Then two PCs do both jobs at once. Each one listens, and each one connects to the other. That is peer to peer, and the same command shows a machine being a server and a client in the same second. {{peers}} Last, you try to reach a PC from outside the office, and the router refuses. That refusal is why peer-to-peer programs need help to find each other on the internet. {{refused}} By the end you can tell which model a service uses, and what each one costs the people who run it. {{choose}}
